label: a6-036-fs-the-compact-open-topology-is-always-metrizable
tail:
### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: Remarks (third bullet)

CLAIM AS WRITTEN: “what this page does prove is that the compact-open and compact-convergence topologies agree for metric X and Y ([[thm-compact-open-equals-compact-convergence]]), which is a different statement and implies no metrizability.”

WHY IT FAILS: The page is a **false‑statement** item that exhibits a counterexample to the claim “the compact‑open topology is metrizable for every metric X and Y”. It does **not** prove the theorem that the compact‑open and compact‑convergence topologies agree for metric X and Y — that is the content of a separate item (`thm-compact-open-equals-compact-convergence`), which is only listed as a dependency (and indeed never used in the proof on this page). The Remark therefore asserts a falsehood about what the present page proves.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT: Remove the sentence or rephrase it to say, e.g., “the library does contain a proof that the compact‑open and compact‑convergence topologies agree for metric X and Y ([[thm-compact-open-equals-compact-convergence]]), but that is a different statement and implies no metrizability”.

---

**What I checked:** the definition of the discrete metric and that it gives the discrete topology; the identification of compact subsets with finite subsets; the equality of the compact‑open and pointwise‑convergence topologies on \(\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{R}}\); the construction showing that any countable family of neighbourhoods of the constant‑0 function fails to be a neighbourhood base (in particular the definition of \(G_k\), the finite‑support argument, the use of \(\mathrm{AC}_\omega\) exactly once via the countable‑union theorem, and the uncountability of \(\mathbb{R}\)); the deduction that the space is not first‑countable and therefore not metrizable; the consistency of all cited dependencies with the claims for which they were cited. No fatal defect was found in the mathematical refutation.

0 fatal, 1 nonfatal
